name: How much do whole-home renovations cost in older Los Angeles homes?

mainEntity.name: Why do older Los Angeles homes often cost more to renovate, and how much extra should I expect?
mainEntity.text: Why do older Los Angeles homes often cost more to renovate, and how much extra should I expect?

acceptedAnswer.text: Older homes often bring more uncertainty, which increases both cost and schedule risk. Once walls are opened, contractors may discover conditions that must be corrected before new finishes can go in. That may include structural reinforcement, sewer or drain replacement, outdated electrical panels, substandard framing, insulation upgrades, or hazardous materials that require special handling. In Los Angeles, many older homes also have past remodels that were not properly documented, which can complicate permitting and inspections. For that reason, older homes usually benefit from a more detailed preconstruction investigation and a larger contingency. The better the upfront assessment, the fewer surprises you will face during demolition.
acceptedAnswer.description: Older Los Angeles homes often cost more to renovate because they may have outdated wiring, old plumbing, hidden damage, asbestos, knob-and-tube wiring, or unpermitted work. These conditions can raise labor, engineering, and permit costs significantly compared with newer homes.
